{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693820525,"sessionID":"ses_e23ec0f2affe163vJ7iXZgj687","part":{"id":"prt_1dc166970001mHN9UMunWw1EBK","messageID":"msg_1dc1647b30013c63WWzibxTwDD","sessionID":"ses_e23ec0f2affe163vJ7iXZgj687","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 111 to the end. web-storefront, the shop's main site, was down for most of the shift, though: about 75–99% of its requests failed until about minute 82, and about 91% failed again from minute 75 to 110.\n\n| Cause | Customer impact | What I did | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| The main node of payments-db (a database) went down before the page | web-storefront ~99% errors (through import-svc), admin-portal ~27% (through geo-svc) | Switched payments-db to its standby at minute 9, then briefly blocked part of its traffic to clear the backlog of retried requests | admin-portal fixed; payments-db healthy by minute 40 |\n| Deploy v78 on risk-svc required a newer encryption protocol (TLS 1.3) that its callers couldn't connect with | partner-api ~4.5% errors, which cost about $800/min at its $18,100/min revenue | Rolled back v78 at minute 31. While the rollback ran, retries overloaded risk-svc and partner-api errors rose to ~43% for about 10 minutes, until a brief traffic block cleared them | partner-api at 0% from minute 47 |\n| import-svc was overloaded, first by retries and then by more steady traffic than 8 copies could handle (about 4,800 requests/sec, up from about 1,800 before the incident) | web-storefront stayed at 75–90% errors | Blocking traffic briefly twice didn't fix it. At minute 75 I increased it from 8 to 20 copies | Healthy by minute 84 (0.05% errors) |\n| New fault at minute 75: deploy v24 on notifications-svc hard-coded its database connection limit to 4 | web-storefront ~91% errors (through ranking-svc) | Rolled back v24 at minute 101, then briefly blocked traffic to clear the retries | web-storefront at 0% from minute 111 |\n\nWhere I lost money:\n- **partner-api, about $11k–$13k:** I should have expected the retry overload on risk-svc. Blocking part of its traffic while the rollback ran would have avoided most of that.\n- **web-storefront, about 20 minutes too long:** I checked its logs for other failing services late. That's why I only traced the notifications-svc fault around minute 86, about 10 minutes after it started. I also spent about 20 minutes on quick traffic blocks at import-svc before seeing it needed more copies.\n\nSpending and leftovers:\n- I left import-svc at 20 copies when I ended the shift because it looked like it needed at least 14. The 12 extra copies cost about $1,600 from minute 78 to the end.\n- No traffic blocks are still on.\n- I didn't apply any fix to a service that didn't need it, so there should be no wasted-fix charges.","time":{"start":1794693818736,"end":1794693820519}}}
